The README prose is guard-shaped, so moving it MEASURES whether each guard reads structure (L-043) or prose — which makes both halves of the brief checkable at once.

decisions.what: Forbade the Q-1 builder from touching test/, and treated the resulting pass/fail list as the deliverable
decisions.why: Which guards break under honest prose IS the measurement this run exists to take. A builder that repairs a failing guard mid-edit destroys the result. Zero broke — so the guards are anchored to structure, not to the padded prose, and the run's premise was half wrong in the useful direction.

decisions.what: Committed with test/node-support-citation.test.js RED, knowingly, and filed the re-cite as Q-7 rather than buying green
decisions.why: That guard's subject is a git pathspec covering test/. Q-4 necessarily edits test/, so the guard cannot be green on this commit — the CI run that would refresh its citation cannot exist until after the push. L-043 and the README section's own standing limit 2 both name this window and both forbid the alternatives (narrowing the pathspec, relaxing the assertion). Recorded as a walked exception, never re-labelled as a pass.

decisions.what: Kept the builder's out-of-scope deletion of J-5's prose allowlist, but did NOT accept its stated rationale
decisions.why: The builder called the allowlist a live silent hole. Measured both arms myself: a FALSE prose count fires on both trees; a TRUE prose count is SILENT on the unfixed tree and FIRES on the fixed one. So the allowlist was not permitting unverified counts while the prose readers lived — it went dead when they were retired, and the deletion converts the section to the Attribution section's existing C7 policy (counts in tables, no digits in prose). Defensible and kept; the justification as written overstated the case, and the real cost — an honest TRUE restatement in prose is now refused — is recorded rather than buried.

decisions.what: Cited run 32400996331 at commit 4b63e91, NOT the newer run 32401050374 at 2014bb9
decisions.why: The README section states its own selection rule — 'the most recent full matrix run against a commit that actually changed src/, bin/, test/, or the workflow itself'. 2014bb9 is more recent and its run is green, but it touched only .swarm/, so it is ineligible under the section's own words. Citing the newest green run would have satisfied the machine guard (the diff would still be empty) while violating the prose rule the guard exists to serve — green bought by reading the check instead of the claim. The builder derived this independently and rejected 2014bb9 for the same reason.

decisions.what: Ratified the builder's departure from the history file's 'Cycle N' labelling — for a better reason than it gave
decisions.why: The builder labelled its entry 'Q-7 (improvement run #6)' because it could not verify a cycle number, and disclosed that a reviewer might prefer 'cycle 3'. The conductor CAN verify it: this is cycle 3. But the file already carries a '## Cycle 3' section from an earlier run, so a bare 'cycle 3' label would collide and make the chronological table ambiguous. The departure is correct; the builder's stated reason (uncertainty) was weaker than the real one (collision).

decisions.what: Accepted the builder's out-of-ask change of 'is preserved verbatim in' to 'is recorded in'
decisions.why: Five of the six history entries are byte-identical relocations of README blockquotes; the sixth was authored directly, because Q-1 retired the blockquote convention it would have been moved from. 'Preserved verbatim' was true of the file when it held five entries and became false the moment a sixth was written. The builder flagged it as beyond the literal ask; it is the smaller of two errors, and the alternative was a knowingly loose claim in a section that is machine-checked for exactly this kind of decay.

decisions.what: Committed with both citation guards RED again, by design, and filed the re-cite as Q-8 rather than buying green
decisions.why: Identical in shape to cycle 2, and predicted in the sealed gate BEFORE dispatch rather than explained afterwards. Q-3 necessarily adds a file under test/, which is inside the pathspec the README cites as its own falsification condition, so the guards cannot be green on this commit — the CI run that would refresh the citation cannot exist until after the push (README standing limit 2). The prediction was then checked: 129 tests / 127 pass / 2 fail, and the two failures are exactly the two predicted. A walked exception, never re-labelled as a pass.

decisions.what: Forbade the builder from editing the four matrix rows, and made that a gate cell rather than a hope
decisions.why: The rows describe a REMOTE run (32400996331 @ 4b63e91) that really did report 124/122/0/2. Adding five tests to this checkout does not falsify a past CI run, but it creates an obvious-looking discrepancy that invites a builder to 'fix' the rows to match the local suite — which would fabricate a CI result that never ran, inside the very section this run is hardening against exactly that decay. Gate cell D1 was authored to fail the item outright if it happened, regardless of a green suite. It did not happen: README.md is absent from the diff entirely.

decisions.what: Reported C7 as an unfixed column instead of letting the C4a/C4b win imply more coverage than it bought
decisions.why: The guard makes a single falsified row fire, and cannot see all four rows falsified together consistently (measured: 5 pass / 0 fail). Closing that needs an anchor outside the document, and both mechanisms — live network provenance, or a committed CI artifact — carry costs the operator should choose, not the swarm. Filed as KI-R6-4 / Q-9. A narrowed hole stated as narrowed is worth more than a closed hole claimed.

decisions.what: Closed Q-2 by discovering its remaining work was a file that has never existed
decisions.why: Q-2 carried 'citations.test.js still untreated' across two cycles of notes. It is a PLAN-time files_hint that was never checked against the tree; `git log --all` for that path is empty and only seven test files have ever been added. The lesson is not about the file — it is that a planning artifact was restated as an observation, twice, and no cycle spent the four seconds to `ls` it. Recorded rather than quietly dropped.

known_issues.desc: The watchdog DONE-guard keys on <target>/REPORT.md EXISTING, which on an improvement run is true from cycle 0 because run #5 wrote it — so swarm-watchdog.timer reads 'all-done / reports-present' and no-ops on every firing, and this run has no watchdog crash recovery (L-037). Recorded ONCE; not to be re-derived (L-045).

Two guards in test/readme-tags.test.js now read the same "Tags on exactly one entry" table row (the renamed multi/single-entry test and the structural replacement for the retired co-occurrence guard). This redundancy was INDUCED BY THE CONDUCTOR's dispatch, which mandated both the re-anchor and a no-shrink floor; the builder disclosed it rather than hiding it. Harmless but not coverage — a candidate consolidation once the Q-5 floor is not the binding constraint.

The README Node-support matrix can still be falsified WHOLESALE: gate cell C7 (cycle 4) changed all four rows together to a self-consistent falsehood (200 tests, 198 pass, 0 fail, 2 skipped) and test/readme-matrix-consistency.test.js stayed SILENT at 5 pass / 0 fail. Per-row arithmetic and cross-row agreement catch a single bad row, a transcription slip, or a partial edit — not a lie told consistently. Closing it requires an anchor outside the document (live network provenance, which would skip in the shallow-CI environment the table describes; or a committed machine-readable CI artifact, which changes what CI is responsible for). Operator's call — Q-9.
